1.pericope_label: For, behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven; and all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble. But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings
debates: Whether the burning day is the last judgment or the fall of Jerusalem
Whether the Sun of righteousness is a personal reference to Christ
Whether going forth is meant historically or generally
outliers: Ellicott denies a personal reference because the word for sun is feminine in Hebrew
Calvin objects that a branch is improper where the figure is stubble
Clarke dates the escape to Pella from the moment the siege was suddenly raised
themes: A day burning like a heated oven
A pillar dark on one side and bright on the other
Flames doubled under an arched roof
Calves let out of the stall

3.pericope_label: And ye shall tread down the wicked; for they shall be ashes under the soles of your feet in the day that I shall do this, saith the Lord of hosts. Remember ye the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded unto him in Horeb for all Israel, with the statutes and judgments
debates: Whether treading down the wicked is done by armies or by believers
Why the law is pressed at the close of prophecy
Whether this verse stands here or last in the book
outliers: Clarke reports three ancient versions that place the verse at the end of the book
Gill blames the traditions of the elders invented in the silent interval
Wesley presses statutes and judgments as forbidding a partial obedience
themes: Ashes under the soles of the feet
A written rule left in place of a living voice
A touchstone for trying the spirits

5.pericope_label: Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord: And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse
debates: Whether Elijah himself is to appear or a prophet in his spirit
Whether the fathers and children are families or generations
Whether the day meant is the fall of Jerusalem or the end of the world
outliers: Gill charges the Septuagint with inserting the Tishbite for the word prophet
Ellicott reads the Baptist denial as a reply to a mistaken question
Keil and Delitzsch renders the last word ban rather than curse
themes: A prophet returning in another man
Four hundred years without a prophet
Fathers ashamed of their children and children of their fathers
A book that will not be left to end on a curse
